text:
carla: Quick sync — we're seeing a perf regression after switching to per-channel INT8 calibration on the 13B baseline. p99 latency up ~18% on short seq (<=64) and throughput down ~10% under small-batch workloads.

brian: ugh. is that the kernel selection path switching to a 'slow' per-channel matmul? any profiler traces? :eyes:

carla: perf-bot posted traces in the thread earlier but TL;DR: runtime chooses the per-channel INT8 kernel for matmuls, but for KV cache miss patterns it falls back to an FP32 path for attention scoring in a few hot loops. the branch mispreds + extra memcopies seem to be the culprit.

perf-bot: profile snapshot (short):
```
trace: matmul_int8_per_channel -> 42%
trace: attention_score_fp32_fallback -> 21%
trace: kv_cache_memcpy -> 13%
```

frank: Are we sure this is about per-channel vs per-tensor and not calibration outliers? per-channel amplifies channel-wise ranges, so one extreme activation can blow the scale and trigger different quant code paths.

eva: From the quality side, per-channel gave ~2.3 BLEU/ROUGE improvement on our eval set vs per-tensor on 4-bit and INT8. But the latency hit is real.

brian: options: 1) keep per-channel but add outlier handling (clipping / percentile trimming) during calibration, 2) revert to per-tensor kernels for short-seq low-batch SLOs, 3) modify kernel selection heuristics to prefer per-tensor at seq<=64 or when KV pattern is heavy.

carla: i prototyped #1: calibrate with 99.9 percentile clipping and it reduces the number of per-channel 'slow-path' hits by ~60% in the microbench. quality drop is ~0.4 pts compared to raw per-channel — still better than per-tensor.

frank: Can you paste the calibration command you used?

carla: sure:
```
python calibrate.py --model 13B --calib-set calib_in_domain.jsonl \
  --mode int8 --per-channel true --clip-percentile 99.9 \
  --out calib_13b_int8_pc_clip99.9.npz
```

carla: Also tried a hybrid: per-tensor for feedforward layers + per-channel for attention proj. That got most quality wins and reduced kernel-pressure.

brian: hybrid sounds promising. though runtime complexity goes up (more kernel variants). we need to ensure kernel selection latency is tiny. maybe precompute per-layer kernel choice at model load time and bake into the runtime plan.

perf-bot: measurement (staged):
```
baseline fp16: throughput = 1000 toks/s, p99 = 45ms
per-channel int8 (no clip): throughput = 900 toks/s, p99 = 53ms
per-channel int8 (clip99.9): throughput = 960 toks/s, p99 = 48ms
per-tensor int8: throughput = 980 toks/s, p99 = 50ms
```

eva: calibration dataset debate: in-domain prompts (prod-like) give best quality but may underrepresent rare outliers. random-language-web corpus catches more activation tails but can lead to over-clip and worse downstream. Thoughts?

frank: i prefer a mixed set: 70% in-domain + 30% high-entropy synthetic prompts (long tails). and keep a small outlier-only pass where we record 99.99th percentile to decide clipping thresholds.

brian: we should also compare per-tensor/pc on a KV-heavy replay (many short queries with cold cache) since runtime fallbacks show up there. Carla, can you run the replay with `--kv-replay`?

carla: yes. scheduled a job now — will include fast/slow seq mixes.

devops-bot: job 17921 queued: calib-replay-13B-int8-pc-clip99.9. ETA 2h.

frank: one more idea: quant-aware KV cache: store cached keys/values in the quantized type and only dequantize into compute when necessary. avoids some memcopies. but requires kernels that accept quantized KV directly. that's medium effort.

brian: +1 to KV-quant path. track as RFC. For now let's prioritize: (A) run hybrid calibration (per-tensor FFN, per-channel attn) with clip99.9, mixed calib dataset, (B) add a runtime precompute of kernel choices at load, (C) run KV-heavy replay.

carla: agreed. i'll post results in ~3h. if anyone wants to add to the replay dataset, DM me the sample prompts.

eva: please log telemetry flags: `quant_mode`, `calib_clip`, `kernel_choice_plan` so we can correlate SLOs in prod.

brian: also add an A/B in Dedicated with canary traffic so we can validate real-world tail latencies before rollout.

frank: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
